editorial.headline: A Job Portal’s Place in Indonesia’s Employment Information Market
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers vacancy and jobseeker-information services, open to full foreign ownership nationally and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity sits in the information layer of the employment market. It covers recording and delivering vacancy information to people seeking work, while giving employers information on jobseekers’ data and competencies. In clear commercial terms, it makes employment information usable for both sides: candidates receive vacancy information, while employers receive relevant data and competency information about candidates. Recording is expressly part of the activity, alongside delivery of vacancy information. The record also includes online delivery through a job portal, making that digital route part of the stated scope itself.

The classification is open at the Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. Its defining feature remains consistent across that range: information flows from available vacancies to jobseekers, and information about jobseekers flows to employers. The record does not frame the activity around a single channel or operating format; it expressly recognises the online job portal as one way it may be carried out. For a founder, the useful boundary is clear: the business is built around recording and communicating employment information between jobseekers and employers.

Nationally, the PMA position is direct. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. That is a full foreign-ownership ceiling: on the national position recorded here, an investor may hold the entire company conducting this activity. The ownership position is not left to implication or general market practice; it is stated plainly in the record. Nationally, this is an open activity for PMA, with foreign ownership permitted up to the full 100% ceiling.

Bali calls for a separate, equally literal reading. The provincial rule permanently blocks PMA registration for all low- and medium-low-risk KBLI activities across the island. This activity is not blocked. Its Bali assessment is OK or Higher Risk, and the recorded reason says that OSS risk at the Besar scale is Medium-High/High; it therefore sits outside the moratorium’s block. The practical conclusion is unambiguous: a foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today. This is an open Bali position in the supplied record, grounded in its stated risk assessment under the provincial rule.
